topic_tag: perpendicular and parallel lines, intersection
subskill: build a perpendicular and a parallel line, intersect them
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, line ℓ passes through the point (5, 6) and is perpendicular to the line 3x − 7y = 2. Line m passes through the point (4, 4) and is parallel to the line 4x − 3y = 9. Lines ℓ and m intersect at point P. To the nearest hundredth, what is the x-coordinate of P ?
explanation: The line 3x − 7y = 2 has slope 3/7, so ℓ has slope −7/3: y = 6 − (7/3)(x − 5). The line 4x − 3y = 9 has slope 4/3, so m is y = 4 + (4/3)(x − 4). Setting them equal: 6 − (7/3)x + 35/3 = 4 + (4/3)x − 16/3, so 53/3 + 4/3 = (11/3)x and x = 57/11 ≈ 5.18. The option "5.38" gives ℓ the slope −3/7 (the original slope with its sign changed but not inverted). The option "5.74" gives ℓ the original slope 3/7 (parallel instead of perpendicular). The option "8.33" gives m the slope −4/3 (sign error reading the slope of 4x − 3y = 9).

topic_tag: absolute-value equation with a linear right side
subskill: split a sum of absolute values into three regions and check each candidate
prompt: What is the sum of all real solutions of the equation |x + 3| + |x − 9| = 1.25x + 5, rounded to the nearest hundredth?
explanation: Split at x = −3 and x = 9. For x < −3 the left side is −2x + 6, so −2x + 6 = 1.25x + 5 gives x = 1/3.25 ≈ 0.31, which is not less than −3, so it is rejected. For −3 ≤ x ≤ 9 the left side is 12, so 12 = 1.25x + 5 gives x = 5.6, which is in the region. For x > 9 the left side is 2x − 6, so 0.75x = 11 gives x ≈ 14.67, which is in the region. The sum is 5.6 + 14.67 ≈ 20.27. The option "20.57" also keeps the rejected candidate 0.31. The option "14.97" treats the left side as ±(2x − 6) (only the two outer cases), adding 0.31 and 14.67 and missing 5.6. The option "8.98" moves 1.25x to the wrong side in the right-hand region (3.25x = 11, x ≈ 3.38) and adds it to 5.6 without checking the region.

topic_tag: literal equation, formula rearrangement with units
subskill: solve s = ut + (1/2)at² for a after a unit conversion
prompt: A car is traveling at 45 kilometers per hour when it begins to speed up with constant acceleration. During the next 5.2 seconds, it travels 86 meters. For an object with initial speed u meters per second and constant acceleration a meters per second squared, the distance s, in meters, that it travels in t seconds is s = ut + (1/2)at². (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters and 1 hour = 3,600 seconds.) To the nearest hundredth, what is the car's acceleration, in meters per second squared?
explanation: 45 km/h = 45,000 m ÷ 3,600 s = 12.5 m/s. Solving s = ut + (1/2)at² for a gives a = 2(s − ut)/t² = 2(86 − 12.5 × 5.2)/5.2² = 2(21)/27.04 ≈ 1.55. The option "1.51" converts the speed with the rounded factor 0.28 m/s per km/h (u = 12.6). The option "3.96" doubles s but not ut, using a = (2s − ut)/t². The option "8.08" divides by t instead of t², as if the formula were s = ut + (1/2)at.

topic_tag: linear models, percent relation between two linear quantities
subskill: set one linear model equal to 1.25 times another
prompt: Two seedlings are measured each week. Seedling A is 12.5 centimeters tall and grows 1.8 centimeters per week. Seedling B is 6.3 centimeters tall and grows 2.6 centimeters per week. Assuming each seedling keeps growing at its constant rate, after how many weeks, to the nearest hundredth, will seedling B be 25% taller than seedling A ?
explanation: After t weeks, A is 12.5 + 1.8t and B is 6.3 + 2.6t. B is 25% taller than A when 6.3 + 2.6t = 1.25(12.5 + 1.8t) = 15.625 + 2.25t, so 0.35t = 9.325 and t ≈ 26.64. The option "11.66" applies the 25% only to A's starting height (6.3 + 2.6t = 15.625 + 1.8t). The option "17.71" applies the 25% only to A's weekly growth (6.3 + 2.6t = 12.5 + 2.25t). The option "51.83" takes the percent of the wrong base, writing A = 0.75B.

topic_tag: linear equation in context with a percent relation
subskill: express one yield as 1.2 times the other and solve the total
prompt: A farm harvested wheat from two fields. Field A has an area of 14.5 hectares, and field B has an area of 22.3 hectares. Field A produced 20% more wheat per hectare than field B did. Together the two fields produced 196.4 metric tons of wheat. To the nearest hundredth, how many metric tons of wheat per hectare did field B produce?
explanation: Let y be field B's yield in metric tons per hectare. Field A's yield is 1.2y, so 14.5(1.2y) + 22.3y = 196.4, that is 39.7y = 196.4 and y ≈ 4.95. The option "4.76" attaches the 1.2 to the wrong field's area (14.5y + 22.3(1.2y) = 196.4). The option "4.86" reads the relation as B producing 20% less than A (B = 0.8A). The option "5.26" reads "20% more" as 0.2 metric ton per hectare more (14.5(y + 0.2) + 22.3y = 196.4).

topic_tag: system of two linear equations in grouped form
subskill: solve a system written in x + y and x − y, then recover y
prompt: If 3(x + y) − 2(x − y) = 11.6 and (x + y) + 4(x − y) = 9.1, what is the value of y, to the nearest hundredth?
explanation: Let u = x + y and v = x − y. Then 3u − 2v = 11.6 and u + 4v = 9.1. From the second, u = 9.1 − 4v, so 27.3 − 12v − 2v = 11.6, v = 15.7/14 ≈ 1.1214 and u ≈ 4.6143. Then y = (u − v)/2 ≈ 1.75 (and x = (u + v)/2 ≈ 2.87). Expanding directly gives x + 5y = 11.6 and 5x − 3y = 9.1 with the same solution. The option "1.96" multiplies only the x by 4 in 4(x − y), getting 5x = 9.1. The option "2.87" is the value of x, not y. The option "6.11" writes −2(x − y) as −2x − 2y, getting x + y = 11.6.

topic_tag: lines, midpoint with an endpoint on a line
subskill: double the midpoint to place an endpoint on a given line
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, point A lies on the line y = 1.5x + 3, point B lies on the x-axis, and the midpoint of segment AB is (4.5, 1.8). What is the x-coordinate of B ?
explanation: Let B = (b, 0). Since (4.5, 1.8) is the midpoint, A = (2(4.5) − b, 2(1.8) − 0) = (9 − b, 3.6). A is on the line, so 3.6 = 1.5(9 − b) + 3, which gives 1.5(9 − b) = 0.6, 9 − b = 0.4, and b = 8.6. The option "8.1" solves 3.6 = 1.5x + 3 by multiplying 0.6 by 1.5 instead of dividing (x = 0.9). The option "5.3" uses A = (4.5 − b, 1.8), subtracting from the midpoint without doubling it. The option "4.6" moves the 3 with the wrong sign (1.5x = 6.6, x = 4.4).

topic_tag: system of two linear equations in context, time zones
subskill: write elapsed local times as d − D and d + D and solve for d
prompt: A nonstop flight leaves city P at 8:55 a.m. local time and lands in city Q at 1:47 p.m. local time on the same day. The return flight leaves city Q at 8:05 a.m. local time and lands in city P at 10:27 p.m. local time on the same day. The two flights take exactly the same amount of time, and the two cities are in different time zones. To the nearest hundredth of an hour, how many hours does each flight take?
explanation: Let d be the flight time and let city Q's clock be D behind city P's. The outbound flight's local times differ by 1:47 p.m. − 8:55 a.m. = 4 h 52 min = d − D. The return flight's local times differ by 10:27 p.m. − 8:05 a.m. = 14 h 22 min = d + D. Adding, 2d = 19 h 14 min, so d = 9 h 37 min ≈ 9.62 hours (and D = 4 h 45 min). The option "9.37" finds 9 h 37 min but writes it as 9.37 hours. The option "9.75" subtracts the minutes the wrong way in 13:47 − 8:55, getting 5 h 08 min, so d = 9 h 45 min. The option "9.57" subtracts the clock times as decimals (13.47 − 8.55 = 4.92 and 22.27 − 8.05 = 14.22) and averages them.

topic_tag: lines, point moving at constant rates meets a line
subskill: substitute linear coordinates in t into a line equation
prompt: A robot moves in a straight path in the standard (x,y) coordinate plane. It starts at the point (−3.5, 2), and each second its x-coordinate increases by 1.5 and its y-coordinate increases by 0.7. To the nearest hundredth of a second, how many seconds after it starts does the robot reach the line 2x + 5y = 30 ?
explanation: After t seconds the robot is at (−3.5 + 1.5t, 2 + 0.7t). Substituting into the line: 2(−3.5 + 1.5t) + 5(2 + 0.7t) = 30, so −7 + 3t + 10 + 3.5t = 30, 6.5t = 27, and t ≈ 4.15. The option "4.89" substitutes the y-expression for x and the x-expression for y (8.9t = 43.5). The option "5.08" moves the constant 3 to the right side with the wrong sign (6.5t = 33). The option "6.69" reads the starting point as (2, −3.5) (6.5t = 43.5).

topic_tag: linear equation with a parameter, compound inequality
subskill: solve for x in terms of k, then turn the range of x into a range of k
prompt: In the equation 3(x − k) + 9.5 = 4x + 4k, k is a constant. The solution x of the equation satisfies 0.7 ≤ x ≤ 5.9. To the nearest hundredth, what is the least possible value of k ?
explanation: Expanding, 3x − 3k + 9.5 = 4x + 4k, so x = 9.5 − 7k. Then 0.7 ≤ 9.5 − 7k ≤ 5.9 gives −8.8 ≤ −7k ≤ −3.6, and dividing by −7 reverses the inequalities: 3.6/7 ≤ k ≤ 8.8/7. The least value of k is 3.6/7 ≈ 0.51. The option "1.26" divides by −7 without reversing the inequalities, so 8.8/7 appears as the lower end. The option "0.72" expands 3(x − k) as 3x − k, giving x = 9.5 − 5k and k ≥ 3.6/5. The option "2.06" moves 4x to the left side with the wrong sign, getting 7x = 7k − 9.5, so x = k − 9.5/7 and k ≥ 0.7 + 9.5/7.

topic_tag: compound linear inequality, "or", complement as an interval
subskill: solve each inequality, then measure the gap neither one covers
prompt: Consider the two inequalities 4 − 3x > 8.6 and 2.5x − 0.8 ≥ 9.6. The set of all real numbers x that satisfy neither inequality is an interval. To the nearest hundredth, what is the length of that interval?
explanation: From 4 − 3x > 8.6, −3x > 4.6, and dividing by −3 reverses the inequality: x < −1.533. From 2.5x − 0.8 ≥ 9.6, 2.5x ≥ 10.4, so x ≥ 4.16. A number satisfies neither inequality when −1.533 ≤ x < 4.16, an interval of length 4.16 + 1.533 ≈ 5.69. The option "5.05" subtracts 0.8 instead of adding it (2.5x ≥ 8.8, x ≥ 3.52). The option "4.57" divides 9.6 by 2.5 before dealing with the 0.8 (x ≥ 3.84 − 0.8 = 3.04). The option "2.63" moves the terms of the first inequality with a sign error, writing 3x < 8.6 − 4 and so x < 1.533, which makes the interval run from 1.533 to 4.16.

topic_tag: linear equation with nested grouping symbols
subskill: distribute through nested brackets and solve
prompt: What value of x satisfies the equation −3.2 − 3[x − 3(x − 0.8)] = 1.5(x + 3.4), to the nearest hundredth?
explanation: Inside the brackets, x − 3(x − 0.8) = x − 3x + 2.4 = −2x + 2.4. Then −3(−2x + 2.4) = 6x − 7.2, so the left side is 6x − 10.4. The right side is 1.5x + 5.1. So 4.5x = 15.5 and x ≈ 3.44. The option "3.07" multiplies only x by 1.5 on the right side (1.5x + 3.4). The option "2.02" moves −3.2 to the right side with the wrong sign (4.5x = 5.1 − 3.2 + 7.2). The option "1.31" does not multiply the 2.4 inside the brackets by −3 (left side 6x − 0.8).

topic_tag: nonlinear systems: two parabolas
subskill: slope through two curve intersections
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, the graphs of y = 4x² − 11x + 2 and y = −3x² + 6x + 9 intersect at exactly two points. To the nearest hundredth, what is the slope of the line that passes through both points of intersection?
explanation: Setting the expressions equal gives 4x² − 11x + 2 = −3x² + 6x + 9, so 7x² − 17x − 7 = 0 and the intersection x-coordinates have sum 17/7. Both points lie on y = 4x² − 11x + 2, and for two points on y = ax² + bx + c the slope between them is a(x₁ + x₂) + b, so the slope is 4(17/7) − 11 = −9/7 ≈ −1.29. (Equivalently, 3(first equation) + 4(second) eliminates x²: 7y = −9x + 42.) The option "-0.78" is run over rise, (x₁ − x₂)/(y₁ − y₂) = −7/9. The option "3.86" comes from moving 6x across without changing its sign (7x² − 5x − 7 = 0, sum 5/7) and then finding the y-values from the second curve: −3(5/7) + 6. The option "8.43" comes from dividing by a = 7 instead of 2a = 14 in the quadratic formula, which doubles both x-values (sum 34/7), and then using the first curve: 4(34/7) − 11.

topic_tag: radical equations
subskill: cube both sides, cubic terms cancel
prompt: For exactly one real number x, the cube root of x³ + 6x² + 3 is equal to x + 2; that is, ∛(x³ + 6x² + 3) = x + 2. To the nearest hundredth, what is x ?
explanation: Cubing both sides gives x³ + 6x² + 3 = (x + 2)³ = x³ + 6x² + 12x + 8. The x³ and x² terms cancel, leaving 3 = 12x + 8, so 12x = −5 and x = −5/12 ≈ −0.42. Because cubing is reversible, this solution needs no check for extraneous roots. The option "-0.25" uses 6 for 2³ (12x + 6 = 3). The option "-0.67" drops the constant 3 after cancelling (0 = 12x + 8). The option "-0.72" expands (x + 2)³ as x³ + 2x² + 4x + 8, which leaves 4x² − 4x − 5 = 0, and takes its negative root.

topic_tag: exponential equations with a common base
subskill: common base leading to a quadratic
prompt: The equation (1/4)^x · 2^(x²) = 2 · 32^x has two real solutions. To the nearest hundredth, what is the positive difference between the two solutions?
explanation: Write every factor as a power of 2: (1/4)^x = 2^(−2x) and 32^x = 2^(5x), so 2^(x² − 2x) = 2^(1 + 5x). Equating exponents gives x² − 7x − 1 = 0. For x² + Bx + C = 0 the solutions differ by √(B² − 4C), so the difference is √(49 + 4) = √53 ≈ 7.28. The option "3.61" writes (1/4)^x as 2^(2x), giving x² − 3x − 1 = 0 and √13. The option "6.71" moves the 1 with the wrong sign, giving x² − 7x + 1 = 0 and √45. The option "5.74" writes 32^x as 2^(x + 5), giving x² − 3x − 6 = 0 and √33.

topic_tag: quadratic equations: vertex and symmetry
subskill: second zero by symmetry, then coefficient
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, the graph of y = ax² + bx + c, where a, b, and c are constants, passes through the points (0, 9) and (2, 0), and its axis of symmetry is the line x = 3.75. To the nearest hundredth, what is the value of b ?
explanation: The zero x = 2 is 1.75 to the left of the axis x = 3.75, so the other zero is 1.75 to the right, at x = 5.5. Then y = a(x − 2)(x − 5.5), and (0, 9) gives 9 = a(−2)(−5.5) = 11a, so a = 9/11. Expanding, b = −a(2 + 5.5) = −7.5(9/11) ≈ −6.14. The option "-6.07" takes the other zero as 3.75 + 2 = 5.75. The option "-5.45" takes it as 2(3.75) + 2 = 9.5. The option "-9.64" uses the axis formula without the 2, −b/a = 3.75, so b = −3.75a, together with the two given points (4a + 2b + 9 = 0 gives a = 18/7).

topic_tag: quadratic equations in context
subskill: sum of two squares, then the quadratic formula
prompt: The side lengths of two square tiles differ by 5 centimeters, and the combined area of the two tiles is 400 square centimeters. To the nearest hundredth of a centimeter, what is the side length of the smaller tile?
explanation: Let s be the smaller side. Then s² + (s + 5)² = 400, so 2s² + 10s + 25 = 400 and 2s² + 10s − 375 = 0. The positive solution is s = (−10 + √(100 + 3000))/4 ≈ 11.42. The option "10.96" divides 2s² + 10s + 25 = 400 by 2 but leaves the 25, giving s² + 5s + 25 = 200. The option "11.69" squares 5 as 10, giving 2s² + 10s + 10 = 400. The option "11.86" drops the 25 from (s + 5)², giving 2s² + 10s = 400.

topic_tag: quadratic equations
subskill: quadratic formula, simplify radical and fraction
prompt: The solutions of the equation 4x² − 4x − 1 = 0 can be written in the form (a ± √b)/c, where a, b, and c are positive integers and c is as small as possible. What is the value of a + b + c ?
explanation: By the quadratic formula, x = (4 ± √(16 + 16))/8 = (4 ± √32)/8. Since √32 = 4√2, x = (4 ± 4√2)/8 = (1 ± √2)/2, so a = 1, b = 2, c = 2 and a + b + c = 5. The option "44" leaves the formula unsimplified, (4 ± √32)/8. The option "14" simplifies the radical but does not reduce the fraction and reads (4 ± 4√2)/8 as a = 4, b = 2, c = 8. The option "11" divides the radicand by 4 instead of dividing the radical by 4, writing (1 ± √8)/2.

topic_tag: exponent rules
subskill: power of a power versus a tower
prompt: The expression (8^3)^2 · 8^(2^3) / 16^(3^2) is equal to 2^n. What is the value of n ?
explanation: (8^3)^2 = 8^6 = 2^18; 8^(2^3) = 8^8 = 2^24; 16^(3^2) = 16^9 = 2^36. So n = 18 + 24 − 36 = 6. The option "15" reads (8^3)^2 as the tower 8^(3^2) = 8^9 = 2^27. The option "18" reads the tower 16^(3^2) in the denominator as (16^3)^2 = 16^6 = 2^24. The option "29" rewrites 16^9 as 2^(4 + 9) = 2^13, adding exponents instead of multiplying.

topic_tag: polynomial identities
subskill: re-centering a cubic
prompt: For all real numbers x, x³ − 8x² + x + 4 = (x − 3)³ + a(x − 3)² + b(x − 3) + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of b ?
explanation: Substitute x = t + 3, so that x − 3 = t. Then (t + 3)³ = t³ + 9t² + 27t + 27, −8(t + 3)² = −8t² − 48t − 72, and the x term contributes t + 3. The coefficient of t is 27 − 48 + 1 = −20, so b = −20. The option "-47" expands (t + 3)³ as t³ + 27, so the cube contributes no t term (0 − 48 + 1). The option "-38" uses 3·3·t instead of 3·3²·t in the cube (9 − 48 + 1). The option "-21" omits the original x term (27 − 48).

topic_tag: nonlinear systems: two parabolas
subskill: vertex of one graph on another
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, the vertex of the parabola y = x² − 6x + c, where c is a constant, lies on the parabola y = −x² + 4x − 1. What is the value of c ?
explanation: The vertex of y = x² − 6x + c has x-coordinate −(−6)/(2·1) = 3 and y-coordinate 9 − 18 + c = c − 9. It lies on y = −x² + 4x − 1, whose value at x = 3 is −9 + 12 − 1 = 2. So c − 9 = 2 and c = 11. The option "-13" takes the vertex x-coordinate as −b/a = 6 (then 36 − 36 + c = −36 + 24 − 1). The option "-49" takes it as b/(2a) = −3 (then 9 + 18 + c = −9 − 12 − 1). The option "2" sets c equal to the vertex's y-coordinate.

topic_tag: quadratic equations: vertex
subskill: two vertices, then the line through them
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, line ℓ passes through the vertex of the parabola y = 3x² − 9x − 4 and through the vertex of the parabola y = −2x² + 4x − 1. What is the y-intercept of line ℓ ?
explanation: The vertex of y = 3x² − 9x − 4 has x = 9/6 = 1.5 and y = 3(2.25) − 13.5 − 4 = −10.75. The vertex of y = −2x² + 4x − 1 has x = −4/(2·(−2)) = 1 and y = −2 + 4 − 1 = 1. The slope of ℓ is (1 − (−10.75))/(1 − 1.5) = −23.5, so its y-intercept is 1 − (−23.5)(1) = 24.5. The option "3.5" puts the first vertex at x = −b/a = 3 (the 2 left out of −b/(2a)). The option "-8.5" puts the second vertex at x = −1 (sign error in −b/(2a)). The option "51.5" computes the first vertex's y-coordinate as c − b²/4 = −4 − 20.25, leaving out the a = 3.

topic_tag: radical equations
subskill: product of square roots
prompt: What is the solution of the equation √(x + 4) · √(x − 1) = 8, to the nearest hundredth?
explanation: For x ≥ 1, √(x + 4) · √(x − 1) = √((x + 4)(x − 1)), so (x + 4)(x − 1) = 64, x² + 3x − 4 = 64, and x² + 3x − 68 = 0. The positive solution is (−3 + √281)/2 ≈ 6.88; the negative solution makes x − 1 negative and is rejected. The option "6.12" expands (x + 4)(x − 1) as x² + 5x − 4. The option "6.39" expands it as x² + 3x + 4. The option "2.27" does not square the 8, solving x² + 3x − 4 = 8.

topic_tag: quadratic equations: sums and products of solutions
subskill: rebuild an equation from two partial copies
prompt: Ana and Ben each tried to solve the same equation of the form x² + bx + c = 0, where b and c are constants. Ana copied c correctly but copied b incorrectly, and the solutions of the equation she wrote were 5 and −6. Ben copied b correctly but copied c incorrectly, and the solutions of the equation he wrote were 1 and 12. What is the value of c − b for the original equation?
explanation: For x² + bx + c = 0, the solutions have product c and sum −b. Ana's c is correct: c = 5(−6) = −30. Ben's b is correct: b = −(1 + 12) = −13. So c − b = −30 − (−13) = −17. The option "11" swaps which value each student copied correctly (b = −(5 − 6) = 1 from Ana, c = 1·12 = 12 from Ben). The option "-43" takes b = 1 + 12 = 13 (sum of solutions without the sign). The option "-31" uses Ana's equation for both values (b = 1, c = −30).

topic_tag: powers of i in a weighted sum
subskill: group the cycle of i, then modulus
prompt: For i = √(−1), let S = 1·i + 2·i² + 3·i³ + 4·i⁴ + ⋯ + 30·i³⁰, the sum of k·iᵏ for k = 1 through 30. The number S can be written as a + bi, where a and b are real numbers. To the nearest hundredth, what is √(a² + b²), the absolute value of S ?
explanation: The powers of i repeat with period 4: i, −1, −i, 1. Each block of four consecutive terms, k = 4m + 1 through 4m + 4, contributes (4m + 1)i − (4m + 2) − (4m + 3)i + (4m + 4) = 2 − 2i. Terms 1 through 28 form 7 blocks, so they sum to 14 − 14i. The leftover terms are 29·i²⁹ = 29i and 30·i³⁰ = −30. So S = −16 + 15i and |S| = √(256 + 225) = √481 ≈ 21.93. The option 21.21 treats the 30 terms as 7.5 blocks (15 − 15i). The option 45.88 reduces i²⁹ to −i. The option 46.49 reduces i³⁰ to +1.

topic_tag: negative rational exponent in a scaling law
subskill: ratio under a power law, invert the exponent
prompt: Biologists model the resting heart rate H, in beats per minute, of a mammal with body mass M kilograms by H = 241M^(−1/4). Under this model, the resting heart rate of animal B is 25% lower than the resting heart rate of animal A, whose mass is 5.5 kilograms. To the nearest hundredth of a kilogram, what is the mass of animal B ?
explanation: H_B/H_A = (M_B/M_A)^(−1/4). Since H_B is 25% lower, H_B/H_A = 0.75, so M_B/M_A = 0.75^(−4) = (4/3)⁴ = 256/81 ≈ 3.160, and M_B = 5.5·256/81 ≈ 17.38 kg. The option 5.91 applies the exponent −1/4 to 0.75 instead of inverting it. The option 13.43 takes the 25% on the wrong base (ratio 0.8). The option 29.33 replaces the fourth power with multiplication by 4.

topic_tag: complex numbers in AC circuits
subskill: complex product over complex sum, real part
prompt: In an alternating-current circuit, the impedance of a component, in ohms, is a complex number a + bi, where a and b are real; its real part a is the resistance. When two components with impedances Z₁ and Z₂ are connected in parallel, their combined impedance is Z = Z₁Z₂/(Z₁ + Z₂). For i = √(−1), a component with Z₁ = 2 + 5i and a component with Z₂ = 6 − 3i are connected in parallel. To the nearest hundredth of an ohm, what is the resistance (the real part) of Z ?
explanation: Z₁Z₂ = (2 + 5i)(6 − 3i) = 12 − 6i + 30i − 15i² = 27 + 24i, and Z₁ + Z₂ = 8 + 2i. Multiplying by the conjugate, Z = (27 + 24i)(8 − 2i)/(8² + 2²) = (216 − 54i + 192i + 48)/68 = (264 + 138i)/68. The real part is 264/68 ≈ 3.88 ohms. The option 3.38 divides 27 by 8 without the conjugate. The option 2.03 is the imaginary part 138/68. The option 1.50 combines the resistances 2 and 6 as if they were real resistors in parallel.

topic_tag: arithmetic series from a remainder condition
subskill: first and last term, count, series sum
prompt: What is the sum of all three-digit positive integers that have a remainder of 2 when divided by 7 ?
explanation: The three-digit integers with remainder 2 on division by 7 are 100 (= 7·14 + 2), 107, …, 996 (= 7·142 + 2). There are 142 − 14 + 1 = 129 terms with average (100 + 996)/2 = 548, so the sum is 129·548 = 70,692. The option 70,144 uses 128 terms. The option 70,785 also includes the two-digit 93. topic_tag: arithmetic sequence from block sums

explanation: Each of the 11th through 20th terms is 10 terms after a matching term in the first block, so it is 10d larger, and the second block sum exceeds the first by 10·10d = 100d. So 100d = 418.5 − 172.5 = 246 and d = 2.46. The first block sum is 10a1 + 45d = 172.5, so 10a1 = 172.5 − 110.7 = 61.8 and a1 = 6.18. The 30th term is a1 + 29d = 6.18 + 71.34 = 77.52. topic_tag: 3 x 3 determinant

topic_tag: precision of measurements in a quotient
subskill: bounds from rounding, least quotient
prompt: The mass of a metal sample is measured as 386 grams, rounded to the nearest gram, and its volume is measured as 41.7 cubic centimeters, rounded to the nearest tenth of a cubic centimeter. The density of the sample is its mass divided by its volume. To the nearest thousandth of a gram per cubic centimeter, what is the least possible actual density of the sample?
explanation: The actual mass is between 385.5 and 386.5 grams and the actual volume is between 41.65 and 41.75 cubic centimeters. A quotient is least when the numerator is least and the denominator is greatest, so the least possible density is 385.5/41.75 ≈ 9.234 g/cm³. The option 9.211 uses ±1 g and ±0.1 cm³. topic_tag: vectors: work as a dot product
subskill: displacement vector, dot product, path independence
prompt: A constant force F = ⟨−11, −2⟩, in newtons, acts on an object as the object moves in the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, where distances are in meters. The object moves from point P(2, −3) to point R(3, −5) and then from R to point Q(−5, 6). The work, in joules, done by a constant force over a displacement d is the dot product F · d. What is the total work, in joules, done by F on the object over the whole trip?
explanation: The work of a constant force depends only on the total displacement, d = Q − P = ⟨−5 − 2, 6 − (−3)⟩ = ⟨−7, 9⟩. So W = F · d = (−11)(−7) + (−2)(9) = 77 − 18 = 59 joules. Equivalently, the legs give F·⟨1, −2⟩ = −7 and F·⟨−8, 11⟩ = 66, and −7 + 66 = 59. The option 95 takes (−2)(9) as +18. The option 43 dots F with Q's position vector. The option 73 adds the leg works as positive amounts.

topic_tag: conditional probability with two independent tests
subskill: Bayes with repeated evidence
prompt: A screening test for a certain condition gives a positive result for 90% of people who have the condition and for 8% of people who do not have it. In a large population, 4% of the people have the condition. A person chosen at random from this population takes the test twice. Given whether the person has the condition, the two results are independent. Both results are positive. To the nearest thousandth, what is the probability that the person has the condition?
explanation: P(condition and two positives) = 0.04·0.9² = 0.0324. P(no condition and two positives) = 0.96·0.08² = 0.006144. So P(condition | two positives) = 0.0324/(0.0324 + 0.006144) ≈ 0.841. The option 0.319 uses one positive result only. The option 0.854 squares the false-positive rate but not the 90%. The option 0.992 ignores the 4% prevalence.

topic_tag: probability of a seating arrangement
subskill: end seat and non-adjacency, conditional count
prompt: Eight people, including Ana, Ben, and Cy, are seated at random in a row of 8 chairs, with every seating equally likely. To the nearest thousandth, what is the probability that Cy sits in one of the two end chairs and Ana and Ben do not sit in chairs next to each other?
explanation: P(Cy in an end chair) = 2/8 = 1/4. Then the other 7 people fill 7 consecutive chairs; Ana and Ben are adjacent in 6 adjacent pairs × 2 orders × 5! of the 7! arrangements, so P(adjacent) = 1440/5040 = 2/7 and P(not adjacent) = 5/7. The probability is (1/4)(5/7) = 5/28 ≈ 0.179. The option 0.188 uses P(not adjacent) = 1 − 2/8 from the full row. The option 0.214 counts only one order of Ana and Ben. The option 0.204 uses 2/7 for Cy's end chair.

topic_tag: expected value of a count
subskill: expected number of empty boxes
prompt: Five balls are placed into 4 boxes. Each ball is placed, independently of the other balls, into one of the 4 boxes chosen at random, with each box equally likely. To the nearest thousandth, what is the expected number of boxes that end up empty?
explanation: For each box, P(box empty) = (3/4)⁵ = 243/1024. The expected number of empty boxes is the sum of these 4 probabilities: 4·243/1024 = 972/1024 ≈ 0.949. (By cases: 600/1024 with exactly 1 empty, 180/1024 with exactly 2, 4/1024 with exactly 3, and 600 + 360 + 12 = 972.) The option 0.237 is one box's probability. The option 0.766 adds the case probabilities without weighting. The option 0.938 omits the 3-empty case.

topic_tag: expected value of a two-stage game
subskill: conditional expectation by branch
prompt: In a game, a player rolls a fair 6-sided die numbered 1 through 6. If the number rolled is 1, 2, or 3, the player must roll the die a second time and keep the second number; otherwise, the player keeps the first number. The player then earns a number of points equal to the square of the number kept. To the nearest hundredth, what is the expected number of points the player earns?
explanation: With probability 1/2 the first roll is 4, 5 or 6 and is kept; the mean square is (16 + 25 + 36)/3 = 77/3. With probability 1/2 the player rerolls and keeps a fresh roll, whose mean square is (1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 + 36)/6 = 91/6. The expected points are (1/2)(77/3) + (1/2)(91/6) ≈ 12.83 + 7.58 = 20.42. The option 20.08 squares the mean kept value 5. The option 15.17 treats the reroll as again 1, 2 or 3. The option 14.58 uses 3.5 instead of 91/6 for the reroll.

topic_tag: matching problem probability
subskill: inclusion-exclusion over fixed points
prompt: Five people each bring one gift to a party. The 5 gifts are then handed out at random, one to each person, with every way of handing them out equally likely. To the nearest thousandth, what is the probability that at least one person receives the gift he or she brought?
explanation: By inclusion-exclusion, P(at least one match) = 1 − 1/2! + 1/3! − 1/4! + 1/5! = 1 − 0.5 + 0.1667 − 0.0417 + 0.0083 = 0.6333 (equivalently, 120 − 44 = 76 of the 120 handouts have a match). The option 0.667 stops after the 1/3! term. The option 0.672 is 1 − (4/5)⁵, which assumes independence. The option 0.700 adds the 1/4! term.

topic_tag: probability in a first-to-k series
subskill: series length, both teams, last game decisive
prompt: Teams A and B play a series of games that ends as soon as one team has won 3 games. Team A wins each game with probability 0.6 and Team B wins each game with probability 0.4; there are no ties, and the results of different games are independent. To the nearest thousandth, what is the probability that the series lasts exactly 4 games?
explanation: The series lasts exactly 4 games when the eventual winner wins game 4 and exactly 2 of the first 3. For A: C(3,2)(0.6)²(0.4)·(0.6) = 3(0.216)(0.4) = 0.2592. For B: 3(0.4)³(0.6) = 0.1152. The total is 0.3744 ≈ 0.374. The option 0.438 uses 1 − P(3 games) − P(5 games) with P(3 games) = 0.6³ only. The option 0.499 uses C(4,3) = 4. The option 0.518 doubles A's value for B.

topic_tag: law of cosines applied twice in a quadrilateral
subskill: diagonal by law of cosines, then a side by law of cosines
prompt: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = 7 meters, BC = 12 meters, the measure of angle ABC is 75°, CD = 9 meters, and the measure of angle ACD is 52°. Points B and D lie on opposite sides of diagonal AC. To the nearest hundredth of a meter, what is the length of AD ? (Note: For any triangle with sides a, b, and c, where C is the angle opposite side c, c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C.)
explanation: In triangle ABC, AC² = 7² + 12² − 2(7)(12)cos 75° ≈ 193 − 43.48 = 149.52, so AC ≈ 12.228. In triangle ACD, the angle at C between AC and CD is 52°, so AD² = AC² + 9² − 2(AC)(9)cos 52° ≈ 149.52 + 81 − 135.51 = 95.01, and AD ≈ 9.75. The option "9.59" rounds AC to 12 before the second step. The option "7.55" uses sin 52° in place of cos 52° in the second step. The option "7.09" uses sin 75° in place of cos 75° in the first step.

topic_tag: perpendicular chords and the radius of a circle
subskill: radius from two perpendicular intersecting chords
prompt: Chords AB and CD of a circle are perpendicular and intersect at point P inside the circle. AP = 5 inches, PB = 8 inches, and CP = 4 inches. To the nearest hundredth of an inch, what is the radius of the circle?
explanation: By the intersecting-chords relationship, AP·PB = CP·PD, so PD = 40/4 = 10 and CD = 14, AB = 13. The center O is on the perpendicular bisector of each chord. The midpoint of CD is 7 − 4 = 3 inches from P along CD, and that offset is the distance from O to line AB (the chords are perpendicular). So O is 3 inches from AB, and AB has half-length 6.5: r = √(6.5² + 3²) = √51.25 ≈ 7.16. (Check with CD: the midpoint of AB is 1.5 from P, so r = √(7² + 1.5²) ≈ 7.16.) The option "7.62" pairs the half-length of CD with the distance to AB, √(7² + 3²). The option "7.76" uses the power of P, r² = AP·PB + OP², but takes OP as 3 + 1.5 instead of √(3² + 1.5²). The option "8.85" forgets to halve the offset, using √(6.5² + 6²).

topic_tag: area of a region between two arcs (annular sector)
subskill: area swept by a blade offset from the pivot
prompt: A windshield wiper arm is 50 centimeters long from its pivot to its tip. The rubber blade is attached along the outer 35 centimeters of the arm, so the blade runs from 15 centimeters to 50 centimeters from the pivot. The arm rotates back and forth through an angle of 118°. To the nearest square centimeter, what is the area of the region of the windshield that the blade wipes?
explanation: The wiped region is the part of a 118° sector of radius 50 that lies outside the 118° sector of radius 15. With θ = 118π/180 ≈ 2.0595 radians, the area is (1/2)θ(50² − 15²) = (1/2)(2.0595)(2,275) ≈ 2,343. The option "2475" subtracts the triangle with two 15-cm sides and a 118° angle, (1/2)(15²) sin 118°, instead of the small sector. The option "2559" subtracts 15 instead of 15². The option "1313" takes 35 as the inner radius, (1/2)θ(50² − 35²).

topic_tag: triangle inscribed in a circle from its arcs
subskill: inscribed triangle area from central angles
prompt: Points P, Q, and R lie on a circle with a radius of 8 meters. The three minor arcs PQ, QR, and RP measure 80°, 130°, and 150°, respectively. To the nearest hundredth of a square meter, what is the area of triangle PQR ?
explanation: Join each vertex to the center O. Because every arc is less than 180°, O is inside the triangle, which splits into three isosceles triangles with two sides of 8 and apex angles 80°, 130°, and 150°. The area is (1/2)(8²)(sin 80° + sin 130° + sin 150°) = 32(0.9848 + 0.7660 + 0.5) ≈ 72.03. The option "80.48" uses half of each arc (40°, 65°, 75°) in this central-angle formula. The option "67.58" finds PQ = 16 sin 40° and QR = 16 sin 65° but uses 65° instead of the 75° inscribed angle at Q between them. The option "51.08" finds PQ = 16 sin 40° and PR = 16 sin 75° but uses 40° instead of the 65° inscribed angle at P between them.

topic_tag: inscribed and circumscribed circles of a right triangle
subskill: distance between incenter and circumcenter
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, a right triangle has vertices (0, 0), (10, 0), and (0, 6). To the nearest hundredth of a coordinate unit, what is the distance between the center of the circle inscribed in the triangle and the center of the circle circumscribed about the triangle?
explanation: The hypotenuse is √(10² + 6²) = √136 ≈ 11.662. The circumcenter of a right triangle is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, (5, 3). The inscribed circle is tangent to both legs, so its center is (r, r), where r = (area)/(semiperimeter) = 30/13.831 = (10 + 6 − √136)/2 ≈ 2.169. The distance is √((5 − 2.169)² + (3 − 2.169)²) ≈ 2.95. The option "4.36" uses r = area/perimeter ≈ 1.085. The option "3.07" takes the circumcenter at the right-angle vertex (0, 0), the orthocenter, giving r√2. The option "3.66" assumes the distance is R − r = 5.831 − 2.169.

topic_tag: dividing a triangle into equal areas with a vertical line
subskill: area of a similar sub-triangle cut by a vertical line
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, a triangle has vertices (0, 0), (11, 0), and (3, 6). The vertical line x = c divides the triangle into two regions of equal area. To the nearest hundredth, what is the value of c ?
explanation: The triangle's area is (1/2)(11)(6) = 33, so each region has area 16.5. The part of the triangle to the left of x = 3 has area (1/2)(3)(6) = 9 < 16.5, so c > 3. To the right of x = c, the region is a triangle with vertices (c, 0), (11, 0), and (c, (6/8)(11 − c)), with area (3/8)(11 − c)². Setting (3/8)(11 − c)² = 16.5 gives (11 − c)² = 44 and c = 11 − √44 ≈ 4.37. The option "4.06" uses the formula for the left region as if it were still a triangle with apex height 2c, (1/2)(c)(2c) = 16.5. The option "3.85" is the x-coordinate of the center of the inscribed circle. The option "3.22" treats the right region as similar to the whole triangle, 11 − 11/√2.

topic_tag: exponential growth and decay acting together
subskill: combining two exponential factors with different periods
prompt: A culture of 1,840 bacteria grows exponentially and, with nothing else acting on it, would double every 3 hours. An antibiotic is added at the start; acting alone, it would reduce the number of bacteria exponentially by 22% every 4 hours. The two effects act together, so their growth and decay factors multiply. To the nearest whole number, how many bacteria are there 7 hours after the start?
explanation: The number after t hours is N(t) = 1,840 · 2^(t/3) · 0.78^(t/4), so N(7) = 1,840 · 2^(7/3) · 0.78^(7/4) ≈ 1,840 · 5.0397 · 0.64759 ≈ 6,003. The option "5741" counts only completed periods for both effects (2 doublings and 1 reduction): 1,840 · 4 · 0.78. The option "5193" uses the 3-hour period in the decay exponent, 0.78^(7/3). The option "4765" counts only the 2 completed doublings but applies the decay continuously, 1,840 · 4 · 0.78^(7/4).

topic_tag: sum of two exponential decay functions
subskill: total of two decaying quantities with different half-lives
prompt: A sample contains 30 grams of substance A, which has a half-life of 4 hours, and 120 grams of substance B, which has a half-life of 16 hours. Each substance decays exponentially and independently of the other. To the nearest hundredth of a gram, what is the total mass of A and B remaining 9 hours later?
explanation: A(t) = 30(1/2)^(t/4) and B(t) = 120(1/2)^(t/16). At t = 9: A = 30(0.5)^2.25 ≈ 6.31 and B = 120(0.5)^0.5625 ≈ 81.25, for a total of about 87.56 grams. The option "86.25" assumes each substance loses mass at a constant rate of half its starting mass per half-life, so A is gone after 8 hours and B = 120(1 − 9/32). The option "80.38" applies the average half-life, 10 hours, to all 150 grams. The option "71.54" uses e^(−t/T) as if each half-life were a time constant.

topic_tag: rational function model with a parameter
subskill: fit a rational model from one point, then solve
prompt: A typing student's speed, in words per minute, after t weeks of practice is modeled by the function W(t) = 70t/(t + k), where k is a positive constant. After 3 weeks of practice, the student types 40 words per minute. According to the model, after how many weeks of practice, to the nearest hundredth, will the student type 59 words per minute?
explanation: From W(3) = 40: 210/(3 + k) = 40, so 3 + k = 5.25 and k = 2.25. Then 70t/(t + 2.25) = 59 gives 70t = 59t + 132.75, so 11t = 132.75 and t ≈ 12.07. The option "14.32" makes a slip in the last step, 70t = 59t + 70(2.25), so t = 157.5/11. The option "21.45" finds k from the reciprocal ratio, k = 3·40/30 = 4. The option "28.16" forgets to subtract 3 when solving for k, using k = 210/40 = 5.25.

topic_tag: piecewise linear function from a table
subskill: distance as area under a piecewise linear speed function
prompt: A cyclist's speed v, in meters per second, t seconds after starting is given at four times in the table below. Between consecutive times listed, the speed changes at a constant rate (so v is a linear function of t on each interval). t (seconds) | 0 | 4 | 10 | 15 ; v (meters per second) | 0 | 12 | 12 | 3. To the nearest tenth of a meter, how far does the cyclist travel from t = 2 to t = 13 ?
explanation: On each piece the distance is the average of the endpoint speeds times the time. v(2) = 6 (halfway from 0 to 12), and on [10, 15] the speed drops 1.8 m/s each second, so v(13) = 12 − 1.8(3) = 6.6. Distance = (6 + 12)/2·2 + 12·6 + (12 + 6.6)/2·3 = 18 + 72 + 27.9 = 117.9 m. The option "120.6" interpolates v(13) from the wrong end, 12 − 1.8(2) = 8.4. The option "112.5" uses the table value 3 at t = 15 as the speed at t = 13. The option "106.5" averages the table speeds over each whole interval and takes the fraction of the interval inside [2, 13]: 24(2/4) + 72 + 37.5(3/5).

topic_tag: sinusoidal function from circular motion
subskill: height of a point on a rotating wheel as a sine function
prompt: A wheel with a radius of 0.8 meter turns counterclockwise at a constant 4 revolutions per second about an axle that is 2.0 meters above the floor. A reflector on the rim is level with the axle and to its right at time t = 0. To the nearest hundredth of a meter, how high above the floor is the reflector at t = 0.29 second?
explanation: The reflector turns through 2π(4) = 8π radians per second, and it starts at the 3 o'clock position moving up, so its height is h(t) = 2.0 + 0.8 sin(8πt). At t = 0.29, 8π(0.29) ≈ 7.288 radians, which is 1.16 revolutions, or 57.6° past the starting position. h ≈ 2.0 + 0.8 sin(57.6°) ≈ 2.0 + 0.675 ≈ 2.68. The option "2.43" uses cosine, as if the reflector started at the top. The option "2.73" treats 4 as radians per second, sin(4·0.29). The option "2.35" treats 4 as seconds per revolution, sin(2π·0.29/4).

topic_tag: logarithmic model (sound level) with an inverse-square law
subskill: decibel levels at a new distance, then combine intensities
prompt: The sound level L, in decibels, of a sound with intensity I is L = 10 log(I/I₀), where I₀ is a fixed reference intensity. The intensity of the sound from a machine is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the machine, and the intensities of two machines running at the same time add. Machine A produces 82 decibels at a distance of 2 meters, and machine B produces 85 decibels at a distance of 3 meters. A worker stands 6 meters from machine A and 4 meters from machine B. To the nearest hundredth of a decibel, what sound level does the worker hear when both machines run?
explanation: Tripling the distance from A divides its intensity by 9, so A's level is 82 − 10 log 9 ≈ 72.46 dB; going from 3 m to 4 m from B divides its intensity by 16/9, so B's level is 85 − 10 log(16/9) ≈ 82.50 dB. Adding intensities: L = 10 log(10^7.246 + 10^8.250) ≈ 82.50 + 10 log(1 + 10^(−1.004)) ≈ 82.91. The option "83.33" rounds the two levels to 72 and 83 decibels before combining. The option "84.62" treats intensity as inversely proportional to the distance (not its square). The option "85.13" scales by the differences in distance (6 − 2 and 4 − 3) instead of the ratios.

topic_tag: rainwater collection, two rainfall rates
subskill: volume from depth, piecewise rate, time to fill
prompt: Rain that falls on a shed roof drains into a rain barrel that holds 55 gallons. The roof covers a horizontal area of 18 feet by 10 feet, and only 80% of the rain that falls on that area reaches the barrel. During a storm, rain falls at a constant rate of 0.30 inch per hour for the first 30 minutes and then at a constant rate of 1.0 inch per hour until the barrel is full. The barrel is empty when the rain begins, and 1 cubic foot of water is 7.48 gallons. To the nearest tenth of a minute, how many minutes after the rain begins does the barrel become full?
explanation: The barrel holds 55 ÷ 7.48 ≈ 7.353 cubic feet. Each inch of rain on 180 square feet delivers 180(1/12)(0.80) = 12 cubic feet to the barrel. In the first 30 minutes, 0.30(0.5) = 0.15 inch falls, delivering 1.8 cubic feet, leaving about 5.553 cubic feet. At 1.0 inch per hour the barrel gains 12 cubic feet per hour, or 0.2 cubic foot per minute, so the rest takes about 27.76 minutes. Total: 30 + 27.76 ≈ 57.8 minutes. The option "56.6" fills the whole barrel at the average of the two rates, 0.65 inch per hour. The option "48.8" counts the first period as delivering 0.30 inch of rain (the hourly rate) instead of 0.15 inch. The option "61.4" treats 30 minutes as 0.30 hour when finding the rain from the first period.

topic_tag: real wage with compounded inflation
subskill: compound two percent increases, ratio of growth factors
prompt: Over a two-year period, Kai's hourly wage rose from $24.80 to $27.90. During the same two years, consumer prices rose 3.4% in the first year and then rose another 6.1% in the second year. Kai's real wage is his hourly wage divided by the level of consumer prices, so it measures how much his wage can buy. To the nearest hundredth of a percent, by what percent did Kai's real wage increase over the two years?
explanation: The wage grew by a factor of 27.90 ÷ 24.80 = 1.125. Prices grew by a factor of (1.034)(1.061) ≈ 1.097074. The real wage grew by a factor of 1.125 ÷ 1.097074 ≈ 1.02545, an increase of about 2.55%. The option "2.74" adds the two price increases to get 9.5% instead of compounding them (1.125 ÷ 1.095). The option "2.79" subtracts the compounded price increase, about 9.71%, from the 12.5% wage increase. The option "2.48" measures the change as a percent of the new real wage (1 − 1.097074 ÷ 1.125).

topic_tag: emissions per occupant-mile comparison
subskill: normalize by fuel economy and occupancy, percent less
prompt: A city compares the carbon dioxide (CO2) emitted per occupant-mile by a commuter car and by a city bus. The car travels 28 miles per gallon of gasoline, and each gallon of gasoline burned emits 8.89 kilograms of CO2. On 70% of the car's commuting trips the driver is alone, and on the other 30% the car carries the driver and one passenger. The bus travels 4.2 miles per gallon of diesel fuel, each gallon of diesel burned emits 10.18 kilograms of CO2, and the bus carries an average of 18 occupants. To the nearest hundredth of a percent, the bus emits what percent less CO2 per occupant-mile than the car?
explanation: The car carries an average of 0.70(1) + 0.30(2) = 1.3 occupants, so the car emits 8.89 ÷ 28 ÷ 1.3 ≈ 0.24423 kilogram per occupant-mile. Bus: 10.18 ÷ 4.2 ÷ 18 ≈ 0.13466 kilogram per occupant-mile. The bus emits (0.24423 − 0.13466) ÷ 0.24423 ≈ 0.4487, or 44.87% less. The option "51.85" uses the gasoline figure, 8.89 kilograms per gallon, for the bus as well. The option "57.59" counts only the driver, using the car's emissions per vehicle-mile. The option "81.37" divides the difference by the bus's figure instead of the car's.

topic_tag: average speed from timestamps, percent over limit
subskill: elapsed time with borrowing, km/h, percent above
prompt: On a highway with a speed limit of 90 kilometers per hour, an average-speed enforcement system records the time at which each car passes two cameras that are 6.8 kilometers apart. One car passed the first camera at 10:14:37 a.m. and the second camera at 10:18:25 a.m. (hours:minutes:seconds). To the nearest tenth of a percent, by what percent did the car's average speed between the two cameras exceed the speed limit?
explanation: The elapsed time is 10:18:25 − 10:14:37 = 3 minutes 48 seconds = 228 seconds. The average speed is 6.8 ÷ 228 × 3,600 ≈ 107.37 kilometers per hour, which exceeds 90 by 17.37, or 17.37 ÷ 90 ≈ 19.3%. The option "7.9" subtracts the seconds without borrowing (37 − 25 = 12 and 18 − 14 = 4, so 4 minutes 12 seconds). The option "30.3" uses 3.48 minutes for 3 minutes 48 seconds. The option "16.2" divides the excess by the car's speed instead of the limit.

topic_tag: percent change in cost of a fixed basket
subskill: quantity-weighted totals, percent change
prompt: A family tracks the monthly cost of a fixed basket of groceries: 3 gallons of milk, 6 dozen eggs, 5 loaves of bread, and 3 pounds of apples. Last year the prices were $3.46 per gallon of milk, $2.76 per dozen eggs, $3.19 per loaf of bread, and $1.24 per pound of apples. This year the prices are $3.91, $3.22, $3.32, and $1.56, respectively. The family buys the same quantities in both years. To the nearest hundredth of a percent, by what percent did the monthly cost of the basket increase?

topic_tag: annual percentage rate of a short-term loan

topic_tag: stair design: risers, treads, stringer length

The stringer is √(112² + 147²) = √34,153 ≈ 184.81 inches. The option "185.29" reads 9 feet 4 inches as 9.4 feet (112.8 inches). The option "176.57" rounds 14.45 down to 14 risers, giving 13 treads. The option "193.26" uses as many treads as risers (15).

topic_tag: distance to lightning from sound delay

From frame 1,046 to frame 1,268 is 222 frame intervals, or 222 ÷ 30 = 7.4 seconds. The distance is 1,166.2(7.4) ≈ 8,629.9 feet ≈ 1.634 miles. The option "1.585" converts the temperature without adding 32 (72°F), giving a speed of 1,131 feet per second. The option "1.624" drops the 1.1 and adds 72 directly (1,159 feet per second).
